title: Moving the Texas Semiconductor Ecosystem to the Next Level
gist: CSIS maps Texas's semiconductor ecosystem, arguing its rise stems from public procurement and layered state/federal incentives (CHIPS Act, $698.3M TSIF) and that durable advantage hinges on power, water, supplier integration and workforce. It catalogs major fab, materials, packaging and AI data-center investments while flagging Chinese overcapacity in foundational chips as a key risk to Texas's analog-heavy base.

insights.claim: CSIS argues Texas's semiconductor rise is not a free-market story but the cumulative result of public procurement (Apollo, Minuteman), state institution building, university investment and private expansion.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Supports thesis that subsidy-driven clusters, not markets alone, determine where chip capacity lands.
insights.quote: Texas’s semiconductor rise is best understood not as a purely free-market success story, but as the cumulative result of public procurement, state-level institution building, university investment, and private sector expansion.

insights.claim: The Texas legislature appropriated $698.3 million for the Texas Semiconductor Innovation Fund (TSIF); as of August 25, 32 grants had been announced representing about 82 percent of available funds.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: State money is largely committed, so incremental state support may require new appropriations.
insights.quote: As of August 25, 32 grants have been announced, representing about 82 percent of total available funds.

insights.claim: Texas's governor's office identifies up to 17 different local and state incentives and grants available to semiconductor companies, a layered system rather than a single program.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Stacked incentives lower project costs and make Texas a preferred siting choice.
insights.quote: The governor’s office identifies up to 17 different local and state incentives and grants available to semiconductor companies.

insights.claim: Semiconductor companies including Texas Instruments, Samsung, NXP, GlobalWafers, X-FAB and Applied Materials have committed to invest more than $61 billion in Texas over the next decade, with at least 13 new investments receiving CHIPS or TSIF support.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Sizable multi-year capex pipeline benefits equipment, materials and construction suppliers.

insights.claim: CHIPS and Science Act direct grants total $39 billion, of which more than $8 billion is going to Texas.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Texas captures a large share of federal chip subsidies.
insights.quote: The CHIPS and Science Act’s $39 billion commitment in direct grants—including more than $8 billion for Texas

insights.claim: CSIS proposes that the key metric of success should be whether public incentives create capabilities the market would otherwise underprovide: resilient supplier networks, advanced packaging, trusted defense production and a skilled labor pipeline.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Offers a lens for judging which subsidized projects create durable value.

insights.claim: Modern fabs can consume up to 100 megawatt-hours of energy per hour, with energy accounting for as much as 30 percent of production costs.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Cheap, reliable power is a decisive cost lever for chip fab siting.
insights.quote: Modern fabs can consume up to 100 megawatt-hours of energy per hour, with energy costs accounting for as much as 30 percent of production costs.

insights.claim: The 2021 Texas grid outages temporarily halted production at Samsung, NXP and Infineon fabs near Austin, and grid reliability remains a constraint as chip and data-center electricity demand grows simultaneously.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Grid stress from concurrent fab and data-center buildout is a supply-disruption risk and a driver of power generation investment.
insights.quote: in 2021, when outages temporarily halted production at Samsung, NXP, and Infineon fabs near Austin

insights.claim: A modern fab uses about 5 million gallons of water per day; Samsung's Taylor plant targets 75 percent water reclamation, and its Austin facility recycled 960 million gallons in 2021 (a 43.5 percent rate).
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Water reuse is a growing capex line and a siting advantage for Texas versus Arizona.
insights.quote: Estimates suggest that a modern fab uses an average of 5 million gallons per day.

insights.claim: Water has historically not been a major constraint for Texas chipmaking, unlike Arizona where limited surface water and aquifer depletion raise persistent concerns.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Relative water security favors Texas over Arizona for future fab siting.

insights.claim: CSIS warns that power and water constraints could become more binding as fabs, data centers and suppliers expand at the same time.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Resource competition between AI data centers and fabs could raise costs or delay projects.
insights.quote: Power and water constraints could become more important as fabs, data centers, and suppliers expand simultaneously.

insights.claim: Texas is projected to become the largest US data center market by 2030 thanks to land, power and a permissive energy regulatory environment.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Supports power, cooling and grid infrastructure demand in Texas.
insights.quote: Texas is projected to become the largest U.S. data center market by 2030
insights.locator: Texas’s Growth in the Semiconductor Value Chain

insights.claim: Announced Texas AI infrastructure includes Google's $40 billion through 2027, the OpenAI-Oracle-SoftBank Stargate flagship in Abilene plus Milam and Shackelford County sites, Microsoft's $1.4 billion in Medina County, and Fermi America's 11-gigawatt Amarillo campus.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Concentrated hyperscaler capex in Texas drives local power and construction demand.

insights.claim: CSIS cautions that proximity of data centers to Texas fabs does not guarantee integration, since operators source advanced chips globally while Texas production mostly serves automotive, industrial and defense markets.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: AI data-center boom may not translate directly into revenue for Texas chipmakers.
insights.quote: geographic proximity alone does not guarantee integration between the two ecosystems

themes.theme: Advanced packaging as the new battleground

insights.claim: As transistor scaling becomes harder and costlier, advanced packaging has become a central competitive arena for performance-intensive chips.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Favors firms and regions building 2.5D/3D packaging capacity.
insights.quote: As further transistor scaling becomes more difficult and expensive, advanced packaging has become a central area of competition for performance-intensive chips.

insights.claim: UT Austin's Texas Institute for Electronics (TIE) received $440 million from the Texas legislature and leads a DARPA program backed by an $840 million grant for an open-access 3D heterogeneous integration prototyping fab, with partners including AMD, Applied Materials, Intel, Micron and Raytheon.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Shared packaging infrastructure lowers risk for partner firms and supports trusted defense supply.

insights.claim: Samsung is building a 2.5D and 3D advanced packaging facility next to its Taylor fab as part of a $17 billion build-out supported by up to $6.4 billion in CHIPS funding.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Onshoring advanced packaging reduces reliance on Asian OSATs.

insights.claim: SpaceX is investing $280 million in its Bastrop semiconductor R&D and packaging facility, tied to Starlink, which will become North America's largest printed circuit board and panel-level packaging facility.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Vertical integration by SpaceX into packaging signals non-traditional entrants into chip supply chains.

insights.claim: Samsung secured $6.4 billion in CHIPS funding for two Taylor fabs producing 4 nm and 2 nm chips within a $37 billion-plus commitment.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Leading-edge foundry capacity onshore in Texas.

insights.claim: Texas Instruments has committed more than $60 billion to seven fabs across Texas and Utah, including four at its Sherman megasite, supported by $1.6 billion in CHIPS funding and up to $8 billion in investment tax credits.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Massive capacity build in foundational analog chips; ITCs materially lower TI's net capex.

insights.claim: GlobalWafers has invested $3.5 billion in the first US high-volume 300 mm wafer fab in Sherman, with plans to reach $7.5 billion depending on market conditions and government support, and received $406 million in CHIPS subsidies.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Domestic wafer supply expansion is conditional on demand and subsidies.

insights.claim: A cluster of mostly Asian specialty chemical suppliers (Sumika, Dongjin Semichem, DSM Semichem, MGC Pure Chemicals) plus equipment makers Applied Materials and Tokyo Electron are expanding in Texas with TSIF or CHIPS support.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Supplier densification can make Texas self-reinforcing for further fab investment.

insights.claim: Coherent is building the world's first 150 mm indium phosphide wafer line at its Sherman facility for optoelectronics used in AI infrastructure, backed by $33 million in CHIPS funding.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Larger InP wafers could lower costs for AI optical interconnects.

themes.theme: China overcapacity risk to foundational chips

insights.claim: Texas's specialization in analog and mixed-signal foundational chips (Texas Instruments, NXP, Infineon) leaves it exposed to Chinese industrial policy aimed at flooding markets with low-cost foundational chips, especially in auto and power semiconductors.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Chinese mature-node overcapacity is a margin risk for TI and peers in cost-sensitive segments.
insights.quote: Beijing has openly pursued this strategy in auto and power semiconductor segments as part of a broader effort to undercut U.S. producers.

insights.claim: Texas accounts for almost 16 percent of the roughly 194,000 US workers in semiconductor and related device manufacturing, with Dallas and Travis counties each above 10,000.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Existing labor depth supports ramp-ups but remains small relative to announced capacity.

insights.claim: Austin Community College's semiconductor programs have graduated 2,856 students, and over 90 percent of current students are incumbent employees upskilling on full wages, with partner companies covering about $380,000 in tuition in 2024.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Employer-funded upskilling models are a template for scaling technician supply.

insights.claim: CSIS warns workforce shortages could slow project ramp-ups if technician and engineering pipelines do not scale with announced investments.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Labor bottlenecks could delay revenue timelines of new fabs.
insights.quote: Workforce shortages could slow project ramp-ups if technician and engineering pipelines do not scale with announced investments.
